label: Roam Research
description: Query and write blocks and pages in a Roam Research graph via its official Backend API.

form.title: Connect Roam Research
form.subtitle: Paste a graph API token to connect one Roam Research graph. What Anton can do with it is fixed by the token's access scope — read-only, or read & edit for writes. Roam has no OAuth, so this is the only supported connection method.

methods.label: Graph API Token
methods.description: Paste an API token generated inside the specific Roam graph you want Anton to access. No OAuth client setup — Roam doesn't offer one. Probing this connector: the Backend API is `POST https://api.roamresearch.com/api/graph/<graph_name>/q` with an `Authorization: Bearer <api_token>` header and an EDN Datalog body such as {"query": "[:find ?e :where [?e :node/title]]"} — that query is verified to return page entities on a working graph. It answers 308 with a `Location` on a per-graph peer host whose subdomain AND port both vary between calls (peer-35:3003, peer-61:3001, peer-46:3000 all observed), so always follow the Location header and never hardcode a peer. Most HTTP clients follow the redirect but STRIP the Authorization header because the hostname changes, so re-attach it on the redirected request or POST straight to the Location URL. Verify with a READ (`/q`) and never with a write: Roam tokens carry a fixed access scope, so a read-only token is a legitimate configuration and a failed write does NOT mean the connection is broken. Read the response BODY, not just the status, because 401 is overloaded. `{"message": "You are not authenticated"}` means the Authorization header was dropped in transit — retry with it re-attached. `{"message": "You don't have read access to <graph>"}` is three-way ambiguous and was reproduced from all three of: a wrong or miscased `graph_name` (it is CASE-SENSITIVE — `mygraph` fails where `MyGraph` succeeds), an unrecognized token, and a valid token whose scope lacks read (append-only). Do not confidently blame one field on that message; ask the user to check the graph name's capitalization and the token's Access Scope. `{"message": "You don't have write access to <graph>"}` on a token whose reads succeed means a read-only scope, which is a working connection — report success. Some malformed tokens instead return 500 with a `java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` body.
methods.how_to:
## Generate a Roam Research graph API token

Roam's Backend API is authenticated per-graph with a static API token — there's no OAuth flow to connect your account as a whole, so you connect one graph at a time.

### Steps

1. Open the Roam graph you want Anton to access at [roamresearch.com](https://roamresearch.com).
2. Click **Settings** (bottom of the left sidebar), then open the **Graph** tab.
3. Scroll to the **API tokens** section and click **+ New API Token**.
4. Give it a name like `Anton`, choose an **Access Scope** (see the note below — pick **read & edit** if you want Anton to write), and confirm.
5. Copy the token shown — it will not be displayed again.
6. Paste it into **API Token** below, and enter the **Graph name** exactly as it appears in your Roam URL (`roamresearch.com/#/app/<graph-name>`) — it is **case-sensitive**, so `MyGraph` and `mygraph` are not interchangeable.

### Notes

- The token only works against the ONE graph it was created in — connect each graph separately if you use more than one.
- Creating API tokens may require a paid Roam plan (Pro or Believer); free graphs may not show the API tokens section.
- An idle graph can take a few seconds to "wake up" on the first request after being closed — a slow first call is normal, not a broken token.
- Roam tokens are **scoped**, and the scope is fixed when you create the token. The dialog's **Access Scope** dropdown offers *read-only*, *read & edit*, and *append-only*. Choose **read & edit** if you want Anton to create or update blocks and pages, or **read-only** if you only want it to read your graph. **Do not choose append-only** — in testing it was refused both reads and writes through the API, so the connection cannot be verified with one.
- A read-only token connects fine and answers queries, but any write Anton attempts fails with `You don't have write access to <graph>`. If you want Anton to write, create a new **read & edit** token; a token's scope cannot be changed after creation.
- Rate limited by Roam (exact quota undocumented) — if you see frequent failures, space out requests.
